defects.summary: THE CLASS IS NOT CLOSED. plan_sources' whole-document refusals are invisible to a scoped --check-current, which then prints a --repin the same generator refuses at exit 1. Both instances are decidable from the lock document alone, contradicting the round's stillOpen claim that every remaining asymmetry is "inherent, NOT lock-decidable".
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:1385 (bundle claimed twice) and :1351 (MAX_SOURCES). _select_sources narrows `extras` BEFORE plan_sources sees them, so a scoped run plans primary+one source and never meets a conflict or an over-cap array; --repin plans the whole document and does. Neither raise is in a *_blocker, and the AST gate is green because both live outside _REPIN_APPLY_PATH.

REPRODUCED, scratchpad/v5/bundleclash.py — 3-source lock, sources[1] hand-edited to also claim bundle 'cms-platform':
  unscoped --check-current -> exit 1, ZERO commands (ERROR: bundle 'cms-platform' is claimed by both ...)
  --check-current --only <third> -> exit 1, printed:
    python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref 66bd3cd5... --repin-source 'file:///.../third-platform@'
  RAN that line verbatim -> exit 1 | ERROR: bundle 'cms-platform' is claimed by both .../cms-platform and .../other-platform

SECOND INSTANCE, scratchpad/v5/maxsources.py — 9 sources (cap 8):
  unscoped -> exit 1, zero commands. --only src0 -> printed `--repin --ref b4535160... --repin-source '.../src0@'`; RAN -> exit 1 | ERROR: 'sources' lists 9 entries; at most 8 are allowed.

This is the bumper's live path: report_drift's own comment records that _agent-guidance builds `fed_check_out` by concatenating one `--check-current --only <registry>` block per drifted source.

defects.summary: ROUND 4 INTRODUCED: _repin_shrink_guard and report_drift ask repin_shrink_blocker different questions, so a `skills` key whose bundle is not in `bundles` re-opens the class — and lands in a permanent dead end with a refusal sentence that is false.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:1075 passes NO `bundles` argument, so the guard compares the WHOLE `existing["skills"]` against the rebuilt document; :2127 narrows `before` to `{bundle for source in read for bundle in source["bundles"]}`. A stale/merge-artifact key for a bundle the lock does not declare is therefore a shrink to the guard and invisible to the report.

REPRODUCED, scratchpad/v5/shrinkasym.py — single-source lock, `skills` given one extra key `ghost/oldskill`, real working-tree drift:
  --check-current -> exit 1, "Re-pin it (after committing the content) with:"
    python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin
  RAN verbatim -> exit 1 | ERROR: ...skills.lock: the re-pin would leave bundle(s) ghost with no skills at all — a bundle directory stopped existing at the commit this would pin

Two problems, not one. (a) The class: report recommends, apply refuses. (b) The sentence asserts something a reader can check and find false — `bundles` is ["adam"]; no directory for `ghost` ever stopped existing, and no --repin can ever make it non-empty, so the refusal is a dead end no generator command clears. The escape the message offers ("decide deliberately that the lock should stop declaring that bundle") is a no-op: the lock already does not declare it.

defects.summary: ROUND 4 INTRODUCED: report_drift applies the shrink reason to SOURCE blocks whose printed command could not cause that shrink, suppressing a remediation the generator accepts at exit 0 — and printing, under one headline, a reason about a different block.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:2177 `blocker = (blocked or repin_source_blocker(...) or shrink)`. `shrink` is computed once over every bundle the run read (:2127), but a source block's command is `--repin --ref <lock ref> --repin-source '<reg>@'`, which anchors the primary and leaves every other source at its own pin — so a shrink in some OTHER source's bundles cannot happen on it. The comment at :2124-2126 states exactly the right scoping rule ("the command it prints holds every other pin with --ref, so those are the only bundles whose content can move") and then does not apply it to the source branch.

REPRODUCED, scratchpad/v5/shrink_overreach2.py — srcA's bundle emptied in its working tree, srcB advanced by a real commit, primary untouched:
  --check-current -> exit 1, printed commands: []  (both blocks suppressed)
  srcB's block reason, verbatim: "the re-pin would leave bundle(s) srcA with no skills at all ..."
  RAN the command srcB's block declined to print:
    --repin --ref 84cf7f6f... --repin-source 'file:///.../srcB@'
    -> exit 0 | Wrote ...: 3 skills
    srcA skills still present: ['srcA/deploy']   srcB advanced: 080850d85c2a (was d86885d1dfc8)

Consequences: a federated bump is stranded behind an unrelated source's registry-side problem with no route the tool offers, and the file's own cross-repo contract fact (3) — "a block's repair belongs to that block" — is broken on the reason side. Note the same lock asked with `--only srcB` does print the command, so the tool contradicts itself between its two supported framings.

defects.summary: ROUND 4 RE-OPENED ROUND-3 D3: the new shrink refusal sends the reader to a repair only a plain generate can perform, appends no restated_sources() clause, and de-federates the lock at exit 0. The round-4 guard test cannot see it because it keys on the literal phrase "plain generate".
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:1054-1061 ends "Fix it where it broke, or decide deliberately that the lock should stop declaring that bundle." Changing `bundles` is impossible on --repin (it inherits them at :2460), so that instruction IS a plain generate — but the sentence never says the words, and test_generate_skills_lock.py:3862 reads `if "plain generate" not in reason: continue`, so test_no_refusal_sends_a_reader_to_a_plain_generate_that_drops_sources skips this refusal entirely. It is the only *_blocker whose text omits the phrase.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v5/shrinkdeadend.py — federated lock, bundles adam+fastmail, one federated source; registry deletes fastmail's last skill:
  --check-current -> exit 1, no command, reason as above; reason contains "plain generate": False; contains "--source": False
  followed it: `--registry <same> --ref <HEAD> --bundles adam` -> exit 0, "Wrote ...: 1 skills"
  sources after: *** GONE ***

The classFix claims "restated_sources() is the single clause every refusal that mentions a plain generate appends, so remediation advice cannot lose the federated array by omission." A refusal that describes a plain generate without naming it is exactly the omission the clause was supposed to make structurally impossible, and the guard is a phrase match rather than a property.

defects.summary: --check's stale remediation names --ref and --source but not --registry or --bundles, and a plain generate inherits neither. Running the printed line verbatim silently re-points the lock at DEFAULT_REGISTRY, narrows it to DEFAULT_BUNDLES, drops the dropped bundle's skills, and exits 0 with --check green afterwards.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:2526 prints `python3 generate_skills_lock.py --ref {ref}{sources_flags}`. `inheriting = verifying or args.repin` (:2419), so on a plain generate `existing = {}` and :2461-2466 fall through to DEFAULT_REGISTRY / DEFAULT_BUNDLES. Only `sources` is restated.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v5/checkremed.py — lock at `Acme/private-registry`, bundles ['custom'], one federated source, made stale:
  --check -> exit 1, printed:
    python3 generate_skills_lock.py --ref 5ba20394... --source 'cms-platform=file:///.../cms-platform@1a1d5123...:skills'
  RAN verbatim -> exit 0 | Wrote ...: 1 skills from Adam-S-Daniel/agentskills@5ba20394...
  registry: Acme/private-registry -> Adam-S-Daniel/agentskills   REPOINTED
  bundles : ['custom'] -> ['adam']                                NARROWED
  skills lost: {'custom/alpha'}

This is precisely the hazard repin_inherit_blocker's own docstring names ("defaulting would silently re-point this lock at another repository ... narrow this lock to ['adam'], dropping every other bundle's skills") — and --check's remediation is the one line in the file that instructs a reader to do it. Pre-existing rather than round-4-introduced, but it is a live answer to "no remediation message advises something whose literal execution loses data", and it is a strictly worse loss than the `sources` omission round 4 spent a commit closing.

defects.summary: --check-format prints a --repin and is not in the "print it only if you would run it" matrix, so round 4's two NEW refusals (unproven sources, lost inheritance fields) now reject the command it recommends. It is the fleet bumper's write trigger, so the failure is a nightly red with no automated exit.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:1679-1681 prints `python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref <ref> --repo <...> -o <...>` under a `FAILED:` verdict — the prefix the bumper greps to set `repin_reason=format` and re-pin.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v5/formatremed.py (digests stripped to bare hex; placeholders filled as the message directs):
  primary pinned at a branch          -> RAN: exit 1 | ERROR: ... pins '...' at 'main', which is not a commit sha
  a source pinned at a branch  (NEW)  -> RAN: exit 1 | ERROR: ... pins a federated source at something that is not a commit sha
  the lock lost 'bundles'      (NEW)  -> RAN: exit 1 | ERROR: ... 'bundles' is missing or is not a non-empty list
  a bundle emptied                    -> RAN: exit 0 (this one is fine)

The fix report's stillOpen note on this path is false in both halves it says it checked by reading: it claims the path "prints a plain generate rather than a --repin" and "emits --source '<spec>' for every source in the document". It prints a --repin and emits no --source at all. So the stated reason for leaving it out of the matrix ("a plain generate has none of the re-pin refusals") does not apply, and round 4 widened the refusal set without re-reading it.

defects.summary: _apply_repin_sources' docstring asserts a byte-identity that 23caaf3 (one commit later) made false, and contradicts the _COMMIT_SHA_RE comment that relies on the opposite.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:1236-1238: "For a ref that is already a 40-hex sha, which is all this generator writes and now all a --repin will read, by-reference and byte-identical are the same thing." 23caaf3 widened _COMMIT_SHA_RE to [0-9a-fA-F]{40}, so an uppercase 40-hex sha is now "already a 40-hex sha" and is NOT preserved — plan_sources re-resolves every inherited source ref (:1379) and writes resolve_ref's lowercase.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v5/upper_source.py — two-source lock, srcB (the UNNAMED source) hand-set to an uppercase sha, `--repin --repin-source '<srcA>@'`:
  before: 4468E99E90CD717FF10BC76B68B220767C2A3EBD
  exit 0
  after : 4468e99e90cd717ff10bc76b68b220767c2a3ebd    BYTE-IDENTICAL: False

The rewrite itself is correct and wanted — the _COMMIT_SHA_RE comment at :419-423 argues for it explicitly ("the re-pin writes resolve_ref's lowercase output back ... the hook's fetch_source branches on ^[0-9a-f]{40}$"). Only the two comments disagree, and the house rule is that a comment must not assert what a reader can check and find false.
